problems.title: Reverse Linked List
problems.description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return the new head.
problems.constraints: 0 <= number of nodes <= 5000, node values fit in a 32-bit integer
problems.optimal_approach: iterative with three pointers prev, curr, next, O(n) time, O(1) space; recursion also works but uses O(n) stack
follow_up_probes: Can you do it recursively and what is the space cost?
How would you reverse only a sublist between positions m and n?

problems.title: Linked List Cycle
problems.description: Given the head of a linked list, determine whether the list contains a cycle.
problems.constraints: 0 <= number of nodes <= 10^4, you may not modify the list
problems.optimal_approach: Floyd's tortoise and hare with slow and fast pointers, O(n) time, O(1) space; a hash set of visited nodes is O(n) space
follow_up_probes: How would you find the node where the cycle begins?
Why are the two pointers guaranteed to meet?

problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problems.description: Merge two sorted singly linked lists into one sorted list by splicing together the nodes of the two lists, and return its head.
problems.constraints: 0 <= length of each list <= 50, values between -100 and 100
problems.optimal_approach: two pointers with a dummy head node, O(n + m) time, O(1) extra space
follow_up_probes: How would you extend this to merge k sorted lists?
Can you do it recursively and what changes in space?

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.description: Given a string containing only the characters ( ) { } [ ], determine whether the brackets are valid: every open bracket is closed by the same type, in the correct order.
problems.optimal_approach: stack of open brackets with a map from closing to opening bracket, O(n) time, O(n) space
follow_up_probes: Can you reject some inputs without a stack?
How would you return the index of the first invalid bracket?

problems.title: Daily Temperatures
problems.description: Given an array of daily temperatures, return an array where answer[i] is the number of days you have to wait after day i to get a warmer temperature, or 0 if there is none.
problems.optimal_approach: monotonic decreasing stack of indices, pop while the current temperature is higher, O(n) time, O(n) space
follow_up_probes: Why is the total time O(n) even with a loop inside a loop?
Can you do it with O(1) extra space by scanning from the right?

problems.title: Min Stack
problems.description: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element, all in constant time.
problems.constraints: operations are always valid, at most 3 * 10^4 calls
problems.optimal_approach: store with each element the minimum so far, or keep a second stack of minimums, O(1) per operation, O(n) space
follow_up_probes: Can you reduce the extra space when the minimum rarely changes?
How would you support getMax as well?

problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.description: Given an m by n grid of 1s (land) and 0s (water), count the number of islands. An island is formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically.
problems.optimal_approach: DFS or BFS flood fill marking visited cells, or union-find, O(m*n) time, O(m*n) worst-case space
follow_up_probes: What is the space cost of recursive DFS on a huge island?
How would you handle a grid that is streamed or too large for memory?

problems.title: Course Schedule
problems.description: There are numCourses courses labelled 0 to numCourses-1 and a list of prerequisite pairs [a, b] meaning you must take b before a. Return whether it is possible to finish all courses.
problems.optimal_approach: detect a cycle in a directed graph using Kahn's topological sort with in-degrees or DFS with colours, O(V + E)
follow_up_probes: How would you return a valid order of courses?
How do you tell a cycle from a diamond-shaped dependency in DFS?

problems.title: Word Ladder
problems.description: Given a begin word, an end word and a word list, return the length of the shortest transformation sequence from begin to end where each step changes exactly one letter and every intermediate word is in the list. Return 0 if none exists.
problems.constraints: 1 <= word length <= 10, 1 <= word list size <= 5000, all words have equal length
problems.optimal_approach: BFS over words treating one-letter differences as edges, using wildcard buckets like h*t to find neighbours, O(N * L^2); bidirectional BFS speeds it up
follow_up_probes: Why BFS and not DFS?
How does bidirectional BFS reduce the search space?

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
problems.description: Given an integer array and an integer k, return the kth largest element in sorted order, not the kth distinct element.
problems.optimal_approach: min-heap of size k in O(n log k), or quickselect in O(n) average and O(n^2) worst case
follow_up_probes: When is quickselect better than a heap?
How would you solve it for a stream of numbers?

problems.title: Top K Frequent Elements
problems.description: Given an integer array and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements in any order.
problems.constraints: 1 <= length <= 10^5, k is valid, the answer is unique
problems.optimal_approach: count with a hash map then use a min-heap of size k in O(n log k), or bucket sort by frequency in O(n)
edge_cases: k equals number of distinct elements
follow_up_probes: How does bucket sort beat the heap here?
How would you do it if the data does not fit in memory?

problems.title: Merge K Sorted Lists
problems.description: Given an array of k sorted linked lists, merge them into one sorted linked list and return it.
problems.optimal_approach: min-heap holding the head of each list, O(N log k) time, or divide and conquer pairwise merging with the same complexity
follow_up_probes: Why is a heap better than merging one list at a time?
What is the space cost of the heap versus divide and conquer?

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.description: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, meaning it uses exactly the same characters with the same counts.
problems.optimal_approach: count characters in a fixed array of 26 or a hash map, O(n) time, O(1) space; sorting is O(n log n)
follow_up_probes: How would you handle Unicode characters?
Why is the array approach O(1) space?

problems.title: Group Anagrams
problems.description: Given an array of strings, group the anagrams together and return the groups in any order.
problems.constraints: 1 <= number of strings <= 10^4, each string length <= 100, lowercase letters
problems.optimal_approach: hash map from a canonical key to a list; the key is the sorted string O(n k log k) or a 26-count tuple O(n k)
follow_up_probes: Which key is faster, sorted string or character counts, and why?
What if the alphabet is large?

problems.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
problems.description: Given a string s, return the longest palindromic substring in s.
problems.optimal_approach: expand around each centre (odd and even) in O(n^2) time and O(1) space; DP is O(n^2) space; Manacher's algorithm is O(n)
follow_up_probes: Why must you try both odd and even centres?
Can you get O(n) and how?

problems.title: Subsets
problems.description: Given an integer array of unique elements, return all possible subsets (the power set). The solution must not contain duplicate subsets.
problems.optimal_approach: backtracking choosing to include or skip each element, or iterating with bitmasks, O(n * 2^n) time
follow_up_probes: How does the approach change if the array has duplicates?
What is the total number of subsets and why?

problems.title: Permutations
problems.description: Given an array of distinct integers, return all possible permutations in any order.
problems.optimal_approach: backtracking with a used array or swapping in place, O(n * n!) time
follow_up_probes: How would you handle duplicate elements without producing duplicate permutations?
Why is O(n * n!) the lower bound?

problems.title: N-Queens
problems.description: Place n queens on an n by n chessboard so that no two queens attack each other, and return the number of distinct solutions.
problems.optimal_approach: backtracking row by row with sets for columns and both diagonals to prune in O(1), or bitmasks
edge_cases: n equals 2 or 3 has no solution
follow_up_probes: How do you detect diagonal conflicts in constant time?
How would you use symmetry to halve the work?

problems.title: 3Sum
problems.description: Given an integer array, return all unique triplets that sum to zero. The solution set must not contain duplicate triplets.
problems.optimal_approach: sort then fix one element and use two pointers for the rest, skipping duplicates, O(n^2) time
follow_up_probes: How do you skip duplicates correctly?
Why can't a hash set beat O(n^2) here?

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.description: Given an array of non-negative integers representing vertical line heights, find two lines that together with the x-axis hold the most water, and return that area.
problems.optimal_approach: two pointers from both ends, always move the pointer at the shorter line, O(n) time, O(1) space
follow_up_probes: Why is it safe to move the shorter line?
Can you prove no better pair is skipped?

problems.title: Trapping Rain Water
problems.description: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where each bar has width 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
problems.optimal_approach: two pointers tracking left max and right max in O(n) time and O(1) space; prefix and suffix max arrays use O(n) space; a monotonic stack also works
follow_up_probes: Why does the smaller side determine the water level?
How would a monotonic stack solve it?

problems.title: Merge Intervals
problems.description: Given an array of intervals [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals and return the non-overlapping intervals that cover all input intervals.
problems.optimal_approach: sort by start then sweep merging with the last interval, O(n log n) time
follow_up_probes: Do touching intervals like [1,2] and [2,3] merge?
How would you insert a new interval into an already merged list?

problems.title: Jump Game
problems.description: Given an array where each element is your maximum jump length from that position, determine whether you can reach the last index starting from the first.
problems.optimal_approach: greedy tracking the furthest reachable index, O(n) time, O(1) space; DP is O(n^2) or O(n) with more space
follow_up_probes: Why does greedy work here when DP also does?
How would you return the minimum number of jumps?

problems.title: Meeting Rooms II
problems.description: Given an array of meeting time intervals [start, end], find the minimum number of conference rooms required.
problems.optimal_approach: sort start times and end times separately and sweep, or use a min-heap of end times, O(n log n)
edge_cases: back-to-back meetings where one ends as another starts
follow_up_probes: Can a meeting starting exactly when another ends share a room?
How would you also output which room each meeting uses?
